q2_gaps: a capitalized, determiner-less bare noun naming a substance/species ('Salt-bloom bloomed in the tide-pools') — proper name vs. mass kind is unresolved: the capitalized-common-noun default is written for definite 'the N' labels, so nothing decides whether this gets a `Name` atom (as parsed, leaving the referent with no kind atom) or a mass-kind/witness encoding

a proper name whose internal kind word is PLURAL ('the Salt-bloom Tide-pools') — the Kestrel River rule licenses a type atom from the kind word inside the name but is singular (`Member <name> <kind>`), while the 'the Wrens' plural-name rule bars `GroupOf`; whether a named plurality is one individual or a group is not settled
review.notes: The copular-with-time-modifier reification of 'the moon was new' (reified state + Experiencer + Time terms + Past, plus the flat `(Past (Member sk_moon_1 new))`) matches the instruction set's exemplar exactly, and the intransitive-subject roles (Patient for the tide coming, the blooming, the overflowing; Agent for the transitive inanimate 'the spring tide filled …') follow the stated natural-process/transitive-subject tests. Coreference across the five sentences (spring tide, tide-pools) reuses symbols correctly and no unstated time is propagated to the undated sentences.
